newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas rallies late, mostly ends higher.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas rallies late, mostly ends higher.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures staged a late short covering rally Tuesday and mostly ended higher in moderate trade, with March the day's only loser on mild weather forecasts this week that cratered the cash.
March eased 0.2 cent to close at $1.964 per million British thermal units after dipping to $1.85 early. April settled 2.9 cents higher at $1.979. Others also ended up.

"We could see a little more upside, but I don't see this contract (March) muscling an expiry over $2. There's not much potential for a significant rally now," said a Texas trader, noting next week's cold likely would not change sentiment.

Most traders agreed forecasts for very mild weather this week crippled the cash and drove NYMEX lower early, while forecasts for colder weather next week helped trigger a later round of short covering. But few expected much more upside.
"The weather (next week) is not enough and it's too late," the Texas trader said, noting comfortable gas stock levels, particularly in the East, as winter soon draws to a close.
Technical traders, while not ruling out more short covering after the 10 percent slide last week, also painted a mostly bearish picture.

"We got oversold and came back (up) a little, but cash is under the screen and should continue to put pressure on the front of the board," a Midwest trader said, adding there was better support in back months.
Chartists saw support in March at $1.85 and then at the contract low of $1.749. Resistance was seen in the $2 area, then at $2.08-2.09 and $2.25-2.30.

On the physical side, Gulf Coast prices skidded almost 30 cents Tuesday to about the $1.80 level. Midcon pipes were off more than 25 cents to the low-to-mid $1.60s. New York city gate gas slumped almost 50 cents to about $2.20.
The 12-month strip rose 1.2 cents to $2.061. NYMEX said an estimated 48,300 Hub contracts traded, about double Friday's revised tally of 24,096. NYMEX March Hub natgas expires Monday, Feb 24.
No NYMEX Permian or Alberta contracts traded Friday.
On the KCBT, March finished 1.4 cents lower at $1.706, while deferreds ended steady to up 1.5 cents. The East/West spread widened by 1.2 cents to 25.8 cents (NYMEX premium).
Physical prices in the Permian basin were more than 20 cents lower at about $1.60.
